summary:
ANIMA's token is an ERC-721 whose every holder gets an ERC-6551 wallet (AgentAccount, an ERC-1167 clone addressed through the canonical registry 0x000000006551c19487814612e58FE06813775758) and whose accountability lives in six standalone registries, because the monolith token is 23,971 of 24,576 EIP-170 bytes. AgentAccount's defining idea is the 'leash': the token owner is never rate-limited and can always rescue funds, while session keys (what an autonomous agent actually runs with) are bounded by the AutonomyPolicy published on the token (perTxWei, calendar-day dailyWei, expiry, allowDelegateCall, allowUnlistedTargets, merkle targetsRoot), by a per-key lifetime cap, by a (target,selector) allowlist namespaced to the granting owner, and by the agent's live status (Paused/Disputed => no session spend). It bumps ERC-6551 state() on every execution AND on every authorisation widening so a buyer's integrity pin catches re-arming; keeps an append-only audit hash chain keccak(prev, chainId, account, signer, to, value, selector, dataHash, op, state, timestamp) replayable by sdk replayAuditLog; refuses ERC-1271 from session keys; and implements ERC-4337 with the rule that the EntryPoint is never a principal (all userOps must enter via executeUserOp so the responsible session key is charged).

The registries: BondVault holds a single-ERC-20 slashable stake per agent with reserve/release (per-module ownership), requestUnbond/cancelUnbond/withdraw (queued collateral stays slashable for UNBONDING_PERIOD and belongs to whoever queued it), and arbiter slash that consumes free then unbonding but never another job's reserved coverage. ReputationRegistry is ERC-8004 feedback plus an 'attested' flag and 'weight' set only by settlement modules, with an O(1) stake-weighted aggregate (attestedSummaryOf) so spam cannot make reputation unreadable. ValidationRegistry is ERC-8004 validation with expiring requests keyed by keccak(requester, requestHash) to defeat squatting, single-answer named validators, PASS_THRESHOLD 50, plus ERC-8126 risk attestations from a separate provider allowlist. AgentHandles binds verifier-attested email/domain/DID/ENS/social/libp2p/phone/API-key handles one-to-one to an agent, stale on transfer or expiry. AnimaRoles is an admin-free ERC-7432 registry that locks the token in place via the token's module hook instead of escrowing it, caps irrevocable roles at 365 days, and refuses to overwrite a live irrevocable role. AnimaBindings is an immutable ERC-8217 bridge to the singleton ERC-8004 registry.

Measured: AgentAccount 10,709 runtime bytes; registries 5,714 / 9,159 / 6,024 / 4,879 / 5,107 / 1,687; accountOf 26,863 gas monolith vs 31,594 diamond; 268 it() cases in test/*.test.ts (docs say 279). All six registries plus the account implementation are deployed on Base Sepolia, Ethereum Sepolia, Unichain Sepolia, Robinhood and BSC testnets (addresses in deployments/*.json), with the owner keys destroyed. One real defect is unmerged: branch codex/fix-high-priority-bug-in-handle-reclamation (a767f7c) fixes AgentHandles releasing a handle while an older attestation is still fresh.

No web UI is minted by the NFT. The 'Sanctuary' is an off-chain Vite SPA on GitHub Pages; AnimaWeb3Renderer is a separate ERC-4804 manual-mode contract serving HTML for /token/{id}/live that imports viem from esm.sh; tokenURI minted by the Sanctuary is a self-contained data: JSON+SVG. Ownership 'verification' is client-side ownerOf(id)==connected address over 1..totalMinted; enforcement is only the contracts' own owner/controller/session checks. For the unified NFT, AgentAccount (adapt), AnimaRoles (reuse/adapt), AgentHandles (adapt, with the fix) and BondVault/ReputationRegistry (adapt) are the carry-overs; ValidationRegistry only with an escrow; AnimaBindings drop.

components.name: AgentAccount
components.purpose: ERC-6551 token-bound account for each agent token: owner is unrestricted; session keys are bounded by the token's AutonomyPolicy, a per-key lifetime cap, a calendar-day cap, a (target,selector) allowlist/merkle root and the agent's live status; keeps an audit hash chain; ERC-1271 for owner only; ERC-4337 via executeUserOp.
key_functions: token() view returns (chainId, tokenContract, tokenId) — extcodecopy at 0x4d (:164)
state() view; owner() view (0 on foreign chain or self-ownership) (:173-186)
isValidSigner(address,bytes) view returns bytes4 (:198)
grantSession(address signer, uint64 validAfter, uint64 validUntil, uint128 spendCapWei) owner-only (:212)
revokeSession(address signer) owner or anima().guardianOf (:232)
setAllowedCall(address target, bytes4 selector, bool allowed) owner-only, bumps state (:247); allowedCall(target,selector) view keyed by current owner (:257)
execute(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation) payable nonReentrant (:273)
executeWithProof(to, value, data, operation, bytes32[] proof) payable nonReentrant (:289)
executeBatch(Call[] calls) payable nonReentrant returns bytes[] (:305)
auditRoot() public bytes32 (:110); event AuditEntry(root, previousRoot, signer, to, value, selector, dataHash, state)
isValidSignature(bytes32,bytes) view — owner's signature only (:444)
validateUserOp(PackedUserOperation,bytes32,uint256) onlyEntryPoint (:463); executeUserOp(PackedUserOperation,bytes32) onlyEntryPoint nonReentrant (:505)
supportsInterface(bytes4) pure: IERC165, IERC6551Account 0x6faff5f1, IERC6551Executable 0x51945447, IERC1271, IERC721Receiver, IERC1155Receiver (:632)
design_decisions: Owner is not on a leash: 'They must be able to rescue a paused or misconfigured agent's funds without asking anyone.' (:376-378)
Session.grantedBy voids keys on sale: 'otherwise a seller keeps a live, funded key on the buyer's wallet, invisible to every integrity check the sale performed.' (:62-65)
Allowlist namespaced by granting owner 'so a buyer inherits an empty allowlist rather than whatever surface the seller opened up.' (:97-99)
setAllowedCall bumps state(): 'A silent widening would let a seller re-arm a dormant key after the pin was taken.' (:243-246)
EntryPoint is never a principal — earlier version let a session key point callData at execute and skip every cap; all 4337 traffic must enter via executeUserOp (:365-371)
Audit chain binds chainId and account 'so a record from one deployment can never be replayed as evidence about another.' (:338-339)
Session keys cannot sign ERC-1271: 'a budget cap means nothing if the key can instead sign an unbounded off-chain order that some other protocol honours.' (:441-443)
Paused/Disputed agent cannot spend: 'This is what makes the guardian's kill switch real rather than advisory.' (:401-402)
Memory-arg duplicate path kept 'line-for-line identical' because sharing calldata/memory needs an external self-call (:538-541) — but merkle branch is missing on the memory path
security_invariants: Owner never rate-limited; session keys always are (SECURITY.md #9)
Session keys cannot produce ERC-1271 signatures (#10)
Paused or disputed agent cannot spend from a session key (#11)
state() increments on every state-changing call (#12)
Audit root append-only and reproducible off-chain (#13)
Account owned by its own token has no owner (#14)
A key granted by a previous owner is dead whatever its expiry says (:395-396)
components.reuse_notes: Best-engineered piece; maps to the GOAL's in-NFT wallet/vault. Adapt: decouple policy/status reads from IAnima (or keep on the unified hub), add ERC-20 spend caps (native-only today), add the merkle branch to the 4337 memory path, decide on OpenZeppelin dependency (SignatureChecker, MerkleProof, ReentrancyGuardTransient), consider pairing with a receive-only vault.

components.name: BondVault
components.purpose: Slashable ERC-20 bond per agent: anyone deposits, only the owner queues withdrawals (slashable during UNBONDING_PERIOD and paid to the queuer), modules reserve/release coverage per job with per-module ownership, arbiters slash free then unbonding, never another job's reserved coverage; slashed value goes to the harmed party.
key_functions: constructor(IERC20 asset, IERC721 agents, uint64 unbondingPeriod, address owner)
setModule(address,bool) / setArbiter(address,bool) onlyOwner
bondOf(uint256) view returns Bond{total,reserved,unbonding,readyAt,unbondTo}
availableCoverage(uint256) view = total - reserved - unbonding; slashableOf = total - reserved; reservedBy(agentId, module)
deposit(uint256 agentId, uint256 amount) nonReentrant (balance-delta, ExactERC20)
requestUnbond(uint256 agentId, uint256 amount) token owner, one pending; cancelUnbond(agentId) by queuer; withdraw(agentId) permissionless after readyAt
reserve(agentId, amount) / release(agentId, amount) onlyModule
slash(uint256 agentId, uint256 amount, address beneficiary, bytes32 reason) onlyArbiter nonReentrant
design_decisions: 'Unbonding stays slashable… Otherwise an agent front-runs its own accountability by withdrawing the moment it knows a job went badly.' (:26-28)
'Slashing cannot consume reserved capital… one failure cascade into everyone else's protection.' (:29-31)
'Coverage is reserved, not merely counted' (:32-33); 'Slashed value is not burned. It routes to the harmed party' (:35-36)
cancelUnbond gated on the queuer, not the holder — a buyer could otherwise re-queue the seller's collateral to themselves (:201-204)
'judge an agent by availableCoverage, never by slashableOf' (:218-219)
UNBONDING_PERIOD 'Must outlast the dispute window of any module that reserves against this vault' (:61-63)
security_invariants: total >= reserved + unbonding
queued collateral stays slashable
slash consumes free before reserved
queued withdrawal pays whoever queued it
one bond cannot back two jobs
escrow clamps release/slash to vault state
standards: none (bespoke); uses OZ Ownable2Step, ReentrancyGuardTransient, SafeCast; ExactERC20 value-conserving transfers
components.reuse_notes: Keep the accounting for any stake/escrow feature; single-ERC-20 and admin-set module/arbiter sets must become constructor-pinned for a no-admin design. Not the holder's asset vault (that is the ERC-6551 account).

components.name: ReputationRegistry
components.purpose: ERC-8004 reputation registry plus provenance: feedback filed by settlement modules on behalf of paying clients is marked attested and weighted by value at stake; an O(1) running aggregate (attestedSummaryOf) is the integrator read path; ERC-8004 getSummary stays byte-compatible and counts everything.
key_functions: giveFeedback(agentId, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash) permissionless
giveAttestedFeedback(agentId, address client, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash, uint128 weight, bytes32 jobId) settlement module only; client != ownerOf
revokeFeedback(agentId, uint64 index) by client; adjusts aggregate
appendResponse(agentId, client, index, responseURI, responseHash) anyone, event-only
getSummary(agentId, address[] clients, tag1, tag2) view O(n) → (count, int128 mean@2dp, 2)
attestedSummaryOf(agentId) view O(1) → (count, weightedMean, totalWeight)
getAttestedSummary(agentId, clients, tag1, tag2) view O(n)
readFeedback / readFeedbackDetail / getResponseCount / getClients / clientCount / getClientsPaged(agentId, offset, limit) / getLastIndex
setSettlementModule(address,bool) onlyOwner; SUMMARY_DECIMALS = 2
design_decisions: 'consumed naively it is a sybil farm: an agent can mint a thousand addresses and rate itself perfect for the price of gas.' (:14-15)
'Faking it costs exactly as much as the jobs are worth.' (:26)
O(1) aggregate because spam on the client list is 'a denial of service against a competitor' (:60-64)
Anyone may respond to feedback; responses are events (:219-221)
Fixed SUMMARY_DECIMALS removes 'an entire class of integration bug' (:49-52)
security_invariants: attested feedback requires a registered settlement module and a non-owner client
weight = min(price, coverage) at the escrow (flash-loan regression)
aggregate maintained on write and revoke
components.reuse_notes: Useful social-layer trust signal; bound valueDecimals (unchecked 10**x overflow for decimals > 79, client-controlled through WorkEscrow.acceptDelivery), pin settlement modules at construction.

components.name: ValidationRegistry
components.purpose: ERC-8004 validation with expiring requests keyed by keccak256(requester, requestHash) (anti-squatting), single answer from the named validator before expiry, 0-100 score with PASS_THRESHOLD 50; plus ERC-8126 agent security attestations from a separate provider allowlist.
key_functions: requestKeyOf(address requester, bytes32 requestHash) pure
validationRequest(validator, agentId, requestURI, requestHash) — 7-day default; validationRequestWithExpiry(..., uint64 expiry)
validationResponse(bytes32 requestKey, uint8 response, responseURI, responseHash, tag) named validator, once
getValidationStatus / hasPassed / requestOf / getSummary(agentId, validators, tag) / getAgentValidations / getValidatorRequests
recordAgentVerification(agentId, uint8 overallRiskScore, bytes32 etv, mcv, scv, wav, wv, summaryProofId) provider only
getLatestRiskScore(agentId) / latestVerificationOf(agentId)
setValidator / setVerificationProvider / setRestrictValidators onlyOwner
design_decisions: Keying by requestHash alone 'is front-runnable… a denial of service with a payout' — namespacing by opener removes the attack while keeping the ERC-8004 event shape (:181-192)
Requests expire so an agent cannot point at 'pending review' forever (:15-18)
Only the named validator may answer, once — no verdict shopping, no revision (:19-21)
Self-validation refused: 'is not validation, it is marketing' (:229)
Security badges always need an allowlisted provider even when the validator market is open (:127-129)
Unanswered requests contribute nothing: 'a validator's silence says something about the validator, not about the agent' (:304-306)
security_invariants: one answer per request
no answer after expiry
validator != agent holder
risk score <= 100
components.reuse_notes: Adapt only if the unified protocol keeps a work/dispute flow; otherwise drop. Carry the opener-namespaced key idea.

components.name: AgentHandles
components.purpose: Verifier-attested off-chain identities (Email, Domain, DID, ENS, Social, MeshPeer, Phone, ApiKeyId) bound to an agent one-to-one; attestations have an evidence hash, optional expiry, are revocable by verifier or current owner, and go stale when the token changes hands or is burned.
key_functions: setVerifier(HandleKind kind, address verifier, bool allowed) onlyOwner — per-kind authorisation
handleKey(HandleKind, string) pure = keccak256(abi.encode(uint8 kind, value))
attest(agentId, kind, string value, uint64 expiresAt, string evidenceURI, bytes32 evidenceHash) returns index — HandleTaken if another agent has a fresh claim
revoke(agentId, index) by attesting verifier or current token owner
handlesOf(agentId) / handleCount(agentId)
isFresh(agentId, index) view — unrevoked, unexpired, ownerAtAttestation == current owner (staticcall-tolerant)
controls(agentId, kind, value) view; agentFor(kind, value) view reverse lookup; claimedBy(bytes32) public
design_decisions: 'a way for a counterparty to check that a given inbox belongs to a given agent, without asking the agent' (:17-19)
'Verification does not survive a sale' — mirrors the token's rule for autonomy (:26-30)
'What a verifier attests to is off-chain and only as good as the verifier' — evidenceHash for audit (:32-34)
Per-kind verifiers: 'an inbox provider should not be able to certify DNS ownership' (:69-70)
Burned token must make the handle reclaimable rather than squat it via ownerOf revert (:208-210)
security_invariants: one handle, one agent (fresh claims only)
attestation stale on transfer/expiry/revoke
only per-kind allowlisted verifiers may attest
components.reuse_notes: Good fit for the social layer (handles shown on the on-chain site, DM routing). Apply unmerged fix a767f7c (branch codex/fix-high-priority-bug-in-handle-reclamation): _hasFreshClaim must return true if ANY matching attestation is fresh and revoke must not clear claimedBy while another is fresh. Prefer on-chain proofs (ENS) over admin-chosen verifiers.

components.name: AnimaRoles
components.purpose: Standalone ERC-7432 roles registry (OPERATOR, PAYER, AUDITOR, TRAINER or any bytes32) for one collection; locks the token in place through the token's module hook instead of escrowing it; irrevocable roles capped at 365 days; no admin.
key_functions: grantRole(Role{roleId, tokenAddress, tokenId, recipient, expirationDate, revocable, data}) owner or role-approved operator; locks token on first role
revokeRole(tokenAddress, tokenId, roleId) grantee always / anyone if expired / owner if revocable
unlockToken(tokenAddress, tokenId) permissionless once activeRoleCount == 0 and now >= lockedUntil
setRoleApprovalForAll(tokenAddress, operator, approved)
ownerOf / recipientOf / roleData / roleExpirationDate / isRoleRevocable / isRoleApprovedForAll (ERC-7432 views)
hasRole(tokenId, roleId, account) view (non-standard convenience)
supportsInterface: 0xd00ca5cf (ERC-7432), ERC-165; constants OPERATOR/PAYER/AUDITOR/TRAINER, MAX_IRREVOCABLE_DURATION = 365 days
design_decisions: External because the token is 605 bytes under EIP-170; 'Measured, not assumed.' (:22-25)
ERC-7432 'IS NOT an extension of ERC-721' — designed for standalone registries (:27-32)
'Locking instead of escrow… The owner keeps the token in their own wallet, it stays visible to every marketplace and indexer, and it simply cannot move while a role is live.' (:34-39)
'Irrevocable roles are capped… a grant the owner cannot end is a lock the owner cannot lift' (:41-45, :65-67)
'Roles do not survive a sale, structurally' because a live role locks the token (:47-49)
Cannot overwrite a live irrevocable role (fix recorded in TESTNET_AUDIT_2026-09-02) (:137-143)
security_invariants: token locked while any role record exists or lockedUntil in future
irrevocable duration <= 365 days
owner cannot revoke or overwrite a live irrevocable role
grantee may always walk away
components.reuse_notes: Admin-free and standards-conformant; only coupling is IAnimaRoleLocking.lockAgent/unlockAgent and being registered as a token module. Adapt the hook name to the unified hub's lock; roles are advisory unless modules consult hasRole.

components.name: AnimaBindings
components.purpose: ERC-8217 immutable binding of an ERC-8004 agent id to a master ERC-721/1155 NFT so control follows the NFT; binder must own both the agent id and the master token; controllerOf resolves to the master's ownerOf.
key_functions: constructor(address identityRegistry)
bind(uint256 agentId, TokenStandard standard, address tokenContract, uint256 tokenId) — permanent; ERC-6909 refused
bindingOf(agentId) view; controllerOf(agentId) view; bindingMetadataValue() view = abi.encodePacked(address(this)); BINDING_METADATA_KEY = 'agent-binding'
design_decisions: 'Bindings are immutable… re-point at another, which is identity laundering with extra steps.' (:53-55)
'The binder must own the master token at bind time… borrow its standing.' (:57-59)
Must own the agent id too, or 'an attacker can pre-bind somebody else's (or the next anticipated) ERC-8004 id permanently' (:87-89)
security_invariants: one binding per agent id, forever
caller owns agentId in IDENTITY_REGISTRY and the master token
components.reuse_notes: Not needed for swap/social/launchpad/vault. Reuse verbatim only if the unified token must appear in the singleton ERC-8004 registry. scripts/deploy.ts:163 deploys it with no constructor arg (stale).

components.name: AnimaWeb3Renderer (context, outside area)
components.purpose: ERC-4804 manual-mode contract serving on-chain HTML for / and /token/{id}/live (owner, ERC-6551 account, tabbed console with wallet connect and a raw simulate-and-execute panel); separate from the token; imports viem from esm.sh.
key_functions: resolveMode() pure returns bytes32('manual')
fallback(bytes calldata path) returns abi.encode(string html)
components.reuse_notes: 22,592 runtime bytes, no ownership gate, external CDN import — the pattern (serve HTML from a contract keyed by token id) is right, the implementation is not self-contained; IPSEITY's Engine/Premises approach is the better base.

standards_implemented: ERC-4337 (PackedUserOperation; EntryPoint v0.7 0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032 wired on testnets)
ERC-8004 Reputation + Validation registries (draft 2025-08-13; validation key namespaced by opener)
ERC-8126 agent security attestations (optional on-chain surface)
Consumed from the token: ERC-5192 lock hook (lockAgent/unlockAgent), ERC-4907 lease, ERC-5646 fingerprint, EIP-712 wallet binding
unique_ideas: Owner-unrestricted / session-leashed asymmetry: the counterparty can read the agent's spending limits (policyOf) before trading with it
Session.grantedBy and owner-namespaced allowlists make a sale structurally void every key and permission the seller set, with no enumeration
ERC-6551 state() bumped on authorisation widening (setAllowedCall/grantSession), not just execution, so an integrity pin catches a dormant key being re-armed
Audit hash chain over every executed call bound to (chainId, account), replayable off-chain (sdk replayAuditLog) — verifiable operating history for a second-hand agent
EntryPoint is never a principal: all 4337 traffic must go through executeUserOp so the session key, not the bundler, is charged
Guardian can revoke a session and pause but never spend or un-pause
Merkle targetsRoot lets an owner commit to a large allowlist in 32 bytes (executeWithProof)

BondVault: coverage reserved not counted, per-module reservation ownership, unbonding stays slashable and belongs to the queuer, slash order free→unbonding never reserved, slashed value paid to the harmed party
Attested vs open reputation with stake-weighted O(1) aggregate; weight = min(price, coverage) so flash-loaned self-hires cannot buy standing
Validation requests keyed by keccak(requester, requestHash) to defeat mempool squatting; single answer from a named validator; expiring requests
ERC-7432 roles that lock the token in place via the token's module hook instead of escrowing it; irrevocable roles capped at a year
Handles one-to-one per agent, per-kind verifiers, stale on transfer, reclaimable after burn via staticcall-tolerant ownerOf
Per-facet immutable ERC-6551 config verified by animaConfigHash rather than paid for with three cold SLOADs (+11,081 gas → +4,731)
weaknesses: AgentAccount: ERC-4337 memory path (_enforceSessionMemory :567-568) lacks the merkle targetsRoot branch present in _enforceSession (:412-418) despite the 'line-for-line identical' comment

AgentAccount: spend caps are native-value only; ERC-20/NFT movement by a session key is bounded only by the (target,selector) allowlist (SPEC.md itself says a msg.value-only cap is 'a spending limit in name only')
AgentAccount: 'rolling' daily cap is a UTC calendar-day bucket shared across all session keys; grantSession does not validate validUntil > validAfter; re-grant resets spentWei

AgentAccount: audit state semantics differ between execute (post-increment) and executeBatch (pre-increment); owner() reverts for a burned token so account assets are stuck; no CREATE/CREATE2 ops; depends on OpenZeppelin

AgentHandles on main releases a handle when the newest attestation expires/revokes even if an older attestation is still fresh — fix exists unmerged on branch codex/fix-high-priority-bug-in-handle-reclamation (a767f7c)

ReputationRegistry._normalise uses unchecked 10**(decimals-2): valueDecimals > 79 overflows silently, and WorkEscrow.acceptDelivery passes a client-chosen ratingDecimals straight through (aggregate poisoning or checked-arithmetic revert blocking settlement)
BondVault is single-ERC-20, no native ETH, one pending unbond per agent; owner can add arbiters who may slash any free collateral to any beneficiary
Four of six registries have an Ownable2Step admin (modules, arbiters, settlement modules, validators, providers, verifiers) — the token's 'immutable, no admin' promise does not extend to them
ValidationRegistry/ReputationRegistry O(n) summaries over unbounded, permissionlessly growable lists (mitigated only by the O(1) attested aggregate and paging)
AnimaRoles roles are advisory: nothing in AnimaAgent or AgentAccount consults hasRole; expired roles must be collected (revokeRole) before unlockToken
AnimaBindings does not write/verify the agent-binding metadata in the ERC-8004 registry; scripts/deploy.ts deploys it with no constructor arg
Test count drift: 268 it() in test/*.test.ts vs 279 claimed in README/SECURITY/DEPLOYMENT; Base Sepolia deployment owner keys destroyed
website_delivery: Not minted by the NFT. Three surfaces: (1) 'Sanctuary' — an off-chain Vite SPA (index.html, src/main.js) published to GitHub Pages by .github/workflows/pages.yml, hard-coding token 0xb3d92c766e3cb356db381feb21958a9ebb974365 and RPC https://sepolia.base.org; (2) contracts/web/AnimaWeb3Renderer.sol — a separate, stateless, ownerless ERC-4804 manual-mode contract (22,592 runtime bytes) whose fallback(bytes path) returns HTML for '/' and '/token/{id}/live' (web3://0x9160be4d943516a2463ac5f3abac5f5cce7975cd:84532/token/{id}/live, also via *.basesep.w3link.io), with a CONNECT WALLET button and a raw simulate-and-execute console; its module script imports viem@2.55.19 from https://esm.sh so the on-chain page still depends on an off-chain CDN and a public RPC; deployed/recorded by scripts/deploy-web3-renderer.ts and .github/workflows/deploy-web3-renderer.yml; (3) tokens minted from the Sanctuary carry a self-contained data:application/json tokenURI with an inline SVG (metadata, not an app). README additionally describes ENS records (com.anima.agent, com.anima.account, contenthash) via the CLI /bind wizard as a naming layer, not storage.
wallet_gating: Client-side and advisory only. Sanctuary: connect() → walletClient.requestAddresses() → switch to Base Sepolia → discover() reads totalMinted and calls ownerOf(id) for ids 1..n, keeping ids whose owner equals the connected address, then renders the 'Command Chamber' for those ids (any id is also inspectable read-only without connecting). No signature challenge, no session cookie, no server. The on-chain renderer page has no gate at all; it relies on simulateContract surfacing the contract revert before the wallet signs. Real enforcement is entirely in the contracts: AnimaAgent._requireOwnerOf / _requireController / isController (owner ∨ live ERC-4907 user ∨ operator at current epoch), AgentAccount._requireOwner and _authorize (owner unrestricted; session keys leashed by policy/status/caps/allowlist; EntryPoint refused), and module/arbiter/verifier allowlists on the registries.
